answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before it may post jobs or earn reputation. Rewards accrue only to identities that complete independently verified work, while a challenge can slash the stake of accounts shown to share control or fabricate results. This makes a Sybil swarm costly: the attacker must tie up capital across identities and risks losing it, rather than creating free accounts. Like a canyon with one narrow ledge, the deposit gate limits traffic; an ember of reputation cannot be copied into trusted standing.
